substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Written under the heteronyms Sen Kuro and Rex Fraction (archival authority Lee Sharks). Drafted and built by Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) in session on 8 November 2026 under Lee Sharks's direction, from ChatGPT's proposal of a framework kernel (evaluated in §6) and on the archive's existing protocols; revised against a review of v0.1 by ChatGPT, a reading of an intermediate build by DeepSeek, a review of v0.2 by ChatGPT, and two rounds of back-projection reader runs (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok and Qwen), each point checked against the files and records before anything was changed.
methodology: Specification composed from the archive's existing protocols, layer by layer, and tested by building its first instance: a builder reads the registry, the capture registry and each record's first seating in git; every claim quotation is asserted against its record; a verifier runs sixteen structural tests, executes the relation policy over the claim graph and reconstructs the framework at stated dates; back-projection v0.1 scores structural presence on two declared scopes, and v1.0 gives scope A to readers who have not seen the records and scores their answers against the graph. falsification_conditions: A framework kernel built to this specification from which a reader given scope A alone cannot reconstruct the framework's must-survive elements at the threshold of #76 (0.85); a claim the kernel binds whose quotation is not in its record or whose hash has drifted; a relation that changes a claim's state on a dimension the policy does not license; an introduction dated earlier than the record's first seating; a rival status with no warranting claim of its body; a kernel whose prose disagrees with its own lists or its graph where the verifier reports agreement.

wiki_article:
The Framework Holographic Kernel (EA-HK-FRAME-01) is a specification by Sen Kuro and Rex Fraction, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 8 November 2026. It defines the holographic kernel of a framework: a small versioned package, written from the archive's registries by its own builder and tested by its own verifier, from which a machine can rebuild a framework's identity, positions, dated development, evidence bodies, claim states, failures, rival and open questions, and check each against the records it cites.

The specification composes protocols the archive already holds. The holographic kernel of #76 supplies the definition and the threshold of reconstruction; the infrastructure kernel of #74 the repository form and back-projection; UKTP (#547) the seed; the Anti-Summary Test (#1610) and the NLCC validity test (#569) the verification; the Claim Status Packet (#1529) claim-local typed state and a relation policy in which each relation licenses change on named dimensions only; MPAI v2.0 (#1677) the sections; the Space Ark (#629) the non-collapse chain, extended with FRAGMENT ≠ WHOLE; and #1602 the columns that keep correspondence, direction and independence apart.

To these it adds: claims held as pointers to quotations bound to a record's hash; corrections kept as three objects, the withdrawn original, the standing correction and the dated withdrawal; introductions attested from a record's first seating in git; a rival framework evaluated on the same evidence bodies and rules; lines of research that state the result that would advance or retreat the framework and what each result moves; two declared reconstruction scopes; and a reader test in which models that have not seen the records rebuild the framework from the kernel alone.

Its first instance is the hologram of Socrates as Orthonym (EA-HK-ORTHONYM-01), Lee Sharks's framework of #123, deposited after it with the framework map as its human-readable component. The drafts v0.1 to v0.4 are recorded with the reviews by ChatGPT and DeepSeek and the two rounds of reader runs that changed them; the second round, on v0.3, gave a mean yield of 0.977 against the threshold of 0.85. The specification was drafted and built by Claude (Anthropic) under Lee Sharks's direction.

defines_concepts.definition: In EA-HK-FRAME-01, the holographic kernel of #76 built at a framework's grain: a small versioned package, written from the archive's registries by its own builder and tested by its own verifier, from which a machine can rebuild a framework's identity, positions, dated development, evidence bodies, claim states, failures, rival and open questions, each element resolving to the record that holds it.

In EA-HK-FRAME-01, a framework's human-readable map and its kernel deposited as one record: the map as the human-readable component, the kernel package as the machine-traversable component, each pointing to the other.

In EA-HK-FRAME-01, what a result of a line of research moves: the claims or proposed extensions it advances, retreats, qualifies or bounds, and what it leaves unchanged; a result reaches a framework's governing claim only along a relation that licenses the change.
